text:
spending around £128k on a car and then being asked to pay extra for a heated steering wheel is ridiculous. i've owned bmws for many years and this one will be my last. i lodged a complaint with bmw and they did not actually address it at all. to me it's simple: this is a bmw, not some brand that should be pushing paid "add ons" on a £128k car.
i even cancelled my order for the updated i7, which was about £146k. bmw eventually added the heated steering wheel to my current car for free, but that completely misses the point. if i wanted cheap junk with chargeable extras, i'd go to a cheap brand instead. meanwhile, mercedes s class includes a heated steering wheel at no extra cost, thank you very much.
so congratulations to whoever thought tacking on another £100 for that option was a smart move. right now i have 3 bmws in the household, and every one of them will be replaced by a mercedes.

text: incredible engineering and technology, absolutely mind blowing.
i have been driving bmw cars for at least 30 years and they have all been great, but i think this one might actually top the list.

the bmw i7 is really outstanding for both comfort and the way it drives. the big all-screen look may be trendy, but at 60, and probably close to your typical buyer age, our crowd likes one button = one function. that is literally my only gribe with this otherwise extraordinary car.
bmw 760, very good comfort, easy to drive, uses little petrol, the car is clearly noticable to others
overall product quality and the impression compared with what i expected

this is probably my 7th or 8th 7 series. while the exterior styling is interesting, the comfort and ergonomics are not at the level of the earlier one. everything has to be operated through the center console, which i do not find safe while driving. the cost-cutting on this kind of vehicle feels ridiculous: the sunroof is gone without any prior notice, the little "pocket" on the left of the steering wheel is gone, the "comfort plus" setting has disappeared, and the seats are much less comfortable with fewer adjustments (for example, the headrest no longer properly supports anything). it is also very disappointing to see the v8 removed and to be forced into a hybrid petrol v6 that does not deliver driving pleasure, etc....
i am very pleased with my new bmw 7 series saloon 750e x drive m sport. the handbook is quite hard to understand when it comes to the automatic parking function.

text: overall it has been a fantastic car so far. i really like the configuration and the level of luxury, and the build feels very solid. it definitely turns heads and has a strong presence on the road, and i enjoy how it drives. my only gripes are with the software. the app itself is excellent, but idrive gives me trouble. a few things are minor but irritating, like my home screen widgets randomly vanishing so i have to re-add them. the main headache is the esim randomly refusing to activate. i do not hold this against the car itself, as it seems like something that could be fixed with an ota update rather than a hardware issue. still, it is a very frustrating bug, and the only way around it has been to cancel my ubigi plan and start over, which results in double billing. please get this fixed asap!

text: the car failed within the first two weeks, and it was another couple of weeks before the local dealer could even look at it. it was fixed, but the service was extremely poor. the loaner was filthy inside and out, with damage on the front passenger wing and door. i could not get into my bmw id for more than a month because there is no mobile reception at my home, and the dealership that sold the car did nothing helpful when i asked. bmw uk responded quickly but their solution was not quite right, so i had to figure out the fix myself. needing to switch off the driver aids every single time i get in is annoying. the actual drive is fantastic, the interior is ahead of the rivals, mpg is excellent with the battery charged and performance is strong, but much weaker when the battery is empty. before this i owned a porsche panamera gts.

text: since buying it, the car has basically lived at the garage. i was able to drive it for about two weeks, and it has then sat in the garage for the past six weeks, with no timeline because parts are still not available. this is the worst car purchase i have ever made. i should have stayed with the mercedes s class. total disaster.
the best car someone can buy.

i am happy with the new car. it is clearly more comfortable and in general more interesting than the older series i had. still, there are some drawbacks i really cannot ignore: - once the speed goes past about 110-120 km/h, the car is not well insulated anymore, wind noise becomes obvious and disturbing even though it has the special package. - at night, the driver's main rearview mirror gives a blurry picture, lights from cars behind and strong light sources look smeared, vertical lines show up and this makes driving harder. - the air conditioning will not run when the ignition is switched off. - there is no way to turn off the lights while the car is on (for example if you just want the ac working in a parking lot). - every single time you start driving you have to switch on the battery conservation function again. - the driver has no glove compartment now. before it was located to the left of the steering wheel. there is also no smaller extra glovebox like on the f01. - the driver's joystick/control stick feels very rigid when choosing left/right/up/down. - the driver's seat fails to go back to where it was before the car was shut down. - the cup holders do not offer cooling or heating at all.
